clue.text: Not seen to be free from moral stigma

definitions.meaning: something unnoticed has gone unobserved by anyone

explanation.surface: Someone whose sins go unnoticed gets to look morally spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unobserved and figuratively unblemished, so it fits each half of the clue.

clue.text: Mountains Monet initially excluded from paintings

indicators.note: excluded from tells us a letter is removed from the paintings word

parts.note: murals are wall paintings

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the painter's name

explanation.surface: Monet's opening is left out of some wall paintings of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are the mountain range dividing Europe from Asia.

clue.text: Mark goes without most of vacation? It's academic

indicators.note: goes without means the mark surrounds, going outside, the holiday word

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: most of means drop the last letter

parts.note: hols is British informal for holidays, a vacation

explanation.surface: A mark lasts without most of a holiday; the point is moot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's academic' looks like the idiom for irrelevant; 'academic' is a noun, a learned person.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a scholar, a learned person working in a university.

clue.text: Boat originally only used on part of 21

indicators.note: originally means take the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: 21 is the rifle, and a trigger is part of a rifle

explanation.surface: A boat was first used only on part of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a canoe fitted with a float projecting from its side.

clue.text: Literally, establish literary Athenian, one with gangster's character

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Literally, establish literary Athenian, one with gangster's character'. TIMON + I + AL and the definition 'character' fit, but no clue word gives the opening TES; the scan matches the text and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Literally, establish literary Athenian, one with gangster's character

clue.text: Duck that may be lucky at the fete?

definitions.meaning: to duck is to plunge briefly under water

definitions.text: that may be lucky at the fete?
definitions.meaning: a lucky ... is a fete game of pulling a prize blind from a tub

explanation.surface: A duck might bring luck at a village fair.
explanation.walkthrough: A lucky dip is a British fete stall where you pull an unseen prize from a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Dip means a quick plunge, like a duck, and names the lucky-dip prize game.

clue.text: It's excellent with chips!

parts.note: reads like praise for a fish supper; really a slang word for excellent that also names a flatfish served with chips

explanation.surface: A diner raves about a meal at the chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: BRILL is British slang (short for brilliant) for excellent, and also a flatfish often fried and eaten with chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang brill means brilliant, and brill is also a flatfish of the kind a chippy fries.

clue.text: Bishop fell over cleaning implement

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: over tells us the word for fell is turned round

parts.note: a fell is high moorland in northern England, so a moor

explanation.surface: A bishop tripped over a broom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for northern upland moor.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a long-handled brush used for sweeping floors.

clue.text: Artless girl attending class having finally changed direction

parts.note: in means present or attending

indicators.note: the last letter, a compass direction, is swapped for a different compass point

parts.note: a genus is a class or category in biology

explanation.surface: An innocent girl goes to class and ends up turning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having finally changed direction' swaps the final S of GENUS (south) for E (east), giving GENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stage role.

clue.text: Final, desperate way to stop youth with desire

indicators.note: to stop means plug, so the way is inserted into the youth

parts.note: a lad is a youth
St is short for street, a way
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A desperate bid to stop a young man's longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch attempt is the final, desperate effort before defeat.

clue.text: Loyal friend waves back, accepting plan right away

indicators.note: the reversed waves take in the shortened plan, holding it inside
back tells us the word for waves is turned round

parts.note: the sea is a mass of waves

indicators.note: right away tells us the letter R, for right, is removed

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map

explanation.surface: A faithful companion waves goodbye after agreeing to a plan at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' reads as a verb of farewell but is a noun here; 'back' gives AES and 'right away' leaves CHAT. Achates is Aeneas's companion in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates is the faithful companion of Aeneas in Virgil, so his name means a loyal friend.

clue.text: Even impoverished farmers have shares in them

definitions.text: Even impoverished farmers have shares in them

parts.words: Even impoverished farmers have shares in them
parts.note: sounds like poor farmers owning stock; really the blades called shares fitted to farm implements

explanation.surface: Even poor farmers own a stake in something.
explanation.walkthrough: A share (ploughshare) is the cutting blade of a plough, so every plough has a share in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Each plough carries a ploughshare, the blade that cuts the furrow, so farmers have shares in these implements.

clue.text: Casserole broken in mails

indicators.note: broken suggests the letters of the following word are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A stew arrives damaged in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a ragout or casserole of game birds, a kind of rich stew.

clue.text: Star-crossed old soldiers in hollow over on island

indicators.note: on places the following construction after the island letter in this across entry
in puts the old soldiers inside the reversed hollow
over tells us the word for hollow is turned round

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded hollow or valley
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Doomed veterans languish in a valley on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star-crossed' comes from Romeo and Juliet; 'over' gives LLED, and 'on' in an across clue means coming after the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Star-crossed lovers are fated to misfortune, which is exactly what ill-omened describes.

clue.text: County type representing canals in art

indicators.note: representing suggests the letters re-present themselves in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone from a county is depicted by canals in paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lancastrian comes from Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lancastrian is a native of Lancashire, a person from that county.

clue.text: Standard rejection of black popular music

indicators.note: rejection here means throwing back, so the music genre is read backwards

parts.note: rap is a popular music genre with roots in Black American culture

explanation.surface: Turning down rap is now the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected level, a synonym of standard.

clue.text: Every year, mount to protect ancient city's grazing land

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for every year

indicators.note: to protect means surround, so the city sits inside the mount word

parts.note: to stage a play is to mount it
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Each year someone climbs to guard an old city's pastures.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is grassland where livestock graze, the same as grazing land.

clue.text: On drug trip these befuddled campers need it

indicators.note: trip suggests the letters of the two words before it stumble into a new order
befuddled tells us the letters of the next word are confused and rearranged

explanation.surface: A druggy trip leaves campers so muddled they need something.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'trip' rearranges ONDRUG into GROUND, 'befuddled' rearranges THESE into SHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof sheet laid under a tent floor is essential camping kit.

clue.text: Publication found on the terraces?

definitions.meaning: terraces are the standing areas at British football grounds where fans watch

explanation.surface: A magazine turns up among football crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: The terraces are the standing areas of British football grounds, where onlookers watch the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spectator is a British weekly, and a spectator is an onlooker in the crowd.

clue.text: Dependent woman in vessel of elaborate appearance

parts.note: sub is short for submarine, a vessel

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the word for elaborate

parts.note: ornate means elaborately decorated in appearance
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A woman inside a fancy-looking boat relies on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a container for the woman, but it is the submarine at the front; 'in' puts her into the word for fancy-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A subordinate is a dependent or underling, one who depends on a superior.

clue.text: Nomad's plot starts to occasion unrest at home

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground

indicators.note: starts means take the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A wanderer's patch seems likely to cause unrest at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': 'Nomad's' reads as 'Nomad is', with the definition alone giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bedouin is a nomadic Arab of the desert, a wanderer with no fixed home.

clue.text: Urge he regularly displayed? How disgusting!

indicators.note: regularly tells us to take every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An urge he keeps showing makes someone recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugh is an exclamation of disgust or revulsion.

clue.text: Discover uranium close to Turkish borders

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
near means close to

indicators.note: borders means take the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Uranium is found close to the Turkish frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or discover it.

clue.text: Not the main action controlled by cabal

parts.note: under means subject to or controlled by
a cabal is a secret plot or intrigue

explanation.surface: A side plot is run by a group of conspirators.
explanation.definitionFit: A subplot or secondary story line runs beneath the main action of a play or novel.

clue.text: One that has stock to go through?

definitions.meaning: a gun has a wooden stock, the butt held against the shoulder
to search hurriedly through, as a burglar ransacks a drawer

explanation.surface: Something that has supplies to get through.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a gun fitted with a stock, and to rifle is to ransack or search through.

clue.text: Gasman's unit another man uses

indicators.note: uses suggests the letters are employed within the words before it, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A gas fitter borrows another man's measuring unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat once used for billing domestic gas supplies.

clue.text: Consumptive heroine caught by ape

parts.note: Mimi, heroine of Puccini's La Boheme, dies of tuberculosis
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sickly heroine is seized by a great ape.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate or copy them.

clue.text: Way question's gripped retired judge — it holds water

indicators.note: gripped puts the question abbreviation inside the road letters

parts.note: the A1 is a major British road, written AI in crosswords
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the judge word is reversed

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: A road question involving a retired judge concerns something holding water.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, read as AI; 'retired' turns REF into FER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquifer is an underground rock layer that holds and yields groundwater.

clue.text: Spirit of Hebridean island so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals the island name is said aloud for the spirit

parts.note: Rhum is a small island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland

explanation.surface: Spirit of a Scottish island, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhum (also spelt Rum) is one of the Small Isles of Scotland's Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane.

clue.text: Provisional note about following season out West

indicators.note: following places the reversed note after the shortened season
out tells us the West letter is thrown out of the season

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: about tells us the note is turned round

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A temporary note about the next season comes from out West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out West' looks like a direction for the whole clue, but it removes W from WINTER, giving INTER; 'about' turns MI into IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes a temporary arrangement made for the time being, the same as provisional.

clue.text: Bondsman knight drowned in lake

indicators.note: drowned in places the knight inside the lake, submerged

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A guarantor in armour sinks in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the computer that draws the numbers for Britain's Premium Bonds, hence 'Bondsman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Premium Bond prize draw machine is the figurative man behind the bonds.

clue.text: Woman of style defending king? Just that

definitions.text: Woman of style defending king? Just that

indicators.note: defending means surrounding protectively, so the king sits inside

parts.note: Mona is a woman's name
chic means stylish
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A stylish lady guards the king, entirely royalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' puts the king between the woman and the style word; 'Just that' turns the whole clue into a description of a royalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchic means supporting or relating to rule by a king, as the defender of a king would be.
